k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_bind.description: Flags a ClusterRole whose declared rules allow the verb(s) bind on roles or clusterroles in rbac.authorization.k8s.io (a '*' in apiGroups, resources or verbs also matches). Such a grant lets any bound subject bind arbitrary Roles/ClusterRoles to any subject, bypassing RBAC escalation prevention to grant permissions the holder does not itself have cluster-wide (or in any namespace it is bound to). Only declared rules are read; bindings, aggregation and resourceNames narrowing are not considered.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_bind.pass_when: No rule combines a matching API group, resource (roles or clusterroles or '*') and verb (bind or '*').
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_bind.fail_when: At least one rule matches the API group, resource and verb (bind on roles or clusterroles), including via '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_bind.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results), e.g. reserved system:/eks: names or rbac-defaults bootstrap roles.

k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_pod_create.description: Flags a ClusterRole whose declared rules allow the verb(s) create on pods in the core API group '' (a '*' in apiGroups, resources or verbs also matches). Such a grant lets any bound subject create Pods, which lets the holder schedule a Pod that mounts any ServiceAccount token, hostPath or privileged context in the namespace and so escalate to that identity or the node cluster-wide (or in any namespace it is bound to). Only declared rules are read; bindings, aggregation and resourceNames narrowing are not considered.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_pod_create.pass_when: No rule combines a matching API group, resource (pods or '*') and verb (create or '*').
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_pod_create.fail_when: At least one rule matches the API group, resource and verb (create on pods), including via '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_pod_create.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results), e.g. reserved system:/eks: names or rbac-defaults bootstrap roles.

k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_secret_read.description: Flags a ClusterRole whose declared rules allow the verb(s) get, list or watch on secrets in the core API group '' (a '*' in apiGroups, resources or verbs also matches). Such a grant lets any bound subject read Secret objects, exposing ServiceAccount tokens, TLS keys and application credentials stored in the scope cluster-wide (or in any namespace it is bound to). Only declared rules are read; bindings, aggregation and resourceNames narrowing are not considered.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_secret_read.pass_when: No rule combines a matching API group, resource (secrets or '*') and verb (get, list or watch or '*').
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_secret_read.fail_when: At least one rule matches the API group, resource and verb (get, list or watch on secrets), including via '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_secret_read.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results), e.g. reserved system:/eks: names or rbac-defaults bootstrap roles.

k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_wildcard_resou.description: Flags a ClusterRole with any rule whose resources entry contains a '*' character (e.g. '*' or 'pods/*') or whose verbs list contains the literal '*'. Wildcard grants silently extend to every current and future resource or verb, including Secrets, exec and RBAC writes, making the ClusterRole far broader than reviewed. apiGroups wildcards alone are not flagged by this variant.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_wildcard_resou.pass_when: Every rule lists explicit resources without '*' and explicit verbs without '*'.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_wildcard_resou.fail_when: Any rule has a resource string containing '*' or a verbs entry equal to '*'.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_wildcard_resou.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.cluster_ad.description: Surfaces every ClusterRoleBinding whose roleRef.name is cluster-admin as a MANUAL review item listing its subjects; it never returns PASS or FAIL. cluster-admin grants unrestricted '*' on all resources cluster-wide, so each holder is effectively a cluster owner and must be individually justified.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.cluster_ad.pass_when: Never PASS: a cluster-admin binding is always returned as MANUAL for owner justification.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.cluster_ad.fail_when: Never FAIL automatically; roleRef.name == 'cluster-admin' yields MANUAL with the subject list.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.cluster_ad.not_applicable_when: When the binding references any role other than cluster-admin, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results) (e.g. system: bootstrap bindings).

k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_c.description: Flags a ClusterRoleBinding that binds at least one non-system User or Group subject (system:authenticated/unauthenticated/serviceaccounts groups count as non-system) to a ClusterRole whose rules grant update or patch on certificatesigningrequests/approval (certificates.k8s.io). Human or broad-group holders of this permission can approve arbitrary CertificateSigningRequests and so mint client certificates for any user or group, including system:masters-equivalent identities. The referenced ClusterRole is looked up in the complete ClusterRole inventory; ServiceAccount subjects and RoleBinding paths are out of scope.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_c.pass_when: The referenced ClusterRole has no rule matching the permission (or the ClusterRole is not present in the inventory).
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_c.fail_when: A non-system User/Group is bound and the referenced ClusterRole grants update or patch on certificatesigningrequests/approval (certificates.k8s.io), including through '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_c.not_applicable_when: When the binding has no non-system User or Group subjects (only ServiceAccounts or reserved system: identities), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_n.description: Flags a ClusterRoleBinding that binds at least one non-system User or Group subject (system:authenticated/unauthenticated/serviceaccounts groups count as non-system) to a ClusterRole whose rules grant get, list or watch on nodes/proxy (core group). Human or broad-group holders of this permission can reach the kubelet API through the API server proxy, which allows command execution in any Pod on the node and bypasses audit of exec. The referenced ClusterRole is looked up in the complete ClusterRole inventory; ServiceAccount subjects and RoleBinding paths are out of scope.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_n.pass_when: The referenced ClusterRole has no rule matching the permission (or the ClusterRole is not present in the inventory).
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_n.fail_when: A non-system User/Group is bound and the referenced ClusterRole grants get, list or watch on nodes/proxy (core group), including through '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_n.not_applicable_when: When the binding has no non-system User or Group subjects (only ServiceAccounts or reserved system: identities), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_p.description: Flags a ClusterRoleBinding that binds at least one non-system User or Group subject (system:authenticated/unauthenticated/serviceaccounts groups count as non-system) to a ClusterRole whose rules grant create on persistentvolumes (core group). Human or broad-group holders of this permission can create a PersistentVolume backed by a hostPath or arbitrary storage and mount node or other tenants' data into a Pod. The referenced ClusterRole is looked up in the complete ClusterRole inventory; ServiceAccount subjects and RoleBinding paths are out of scope.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_p.pass_when: The referenced ClusterRole has no rule matching the permission (or the ClusterRole is not present in the inventory).
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_p.fail_when: A non-system User/Group is bound and the referenced ClusterRole grants create on persistentvolumes (core group), including through '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_p.not_applicable_when: When the binding has no non-system User or Group subjects (only ServiceAccounts or reserved system: identities), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_s.description: Flags a ClusterRoleBinding that binds at least one non-system User or Group subject (system:authenticated/unauthenticated/serviceaccounts groups count as non-system) to a ClusterRole whose rules grant create on serviceaccounts/token (core group). Human or broad-group holders of this permission can mint fresh tokens for any ServiceAccount, impersonating privileged controller identities. The referenced ClusterRole is looked up in the complete ClusterRole inventory; ServiceAccount subjects and RoleBinding paths are out of scope.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_s.pass_when: The referenced ClusterRole has no rule matching the permission (or the ClusterRole is not present in the inventory).
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_s.fail_when: A non-system User/Group is bound and the referenced ClusterRole grants create on serviceaccounts/token (core group), including through '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_s.not_applicable_when: When the binding has no non-system User or Group subjects (only ServiceAccounts or reserved system: identities), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_w.description: Flags a ClusterRoleBinding that binds at least one non-system User or Group subject (system:authenticated/unauthenticated/serviceaccounts groups count as non-system) to a ClusterRole whose rules grant create, update or delete on validatingwebhookconfigurations/mutatingwebhookconfigurations (admissionregistration.k8s.io). Human or broad-group holders of this permission can register or alter admission webhooks that can intercept, mutate or block every API write, including injecting containers or reading submitted Secrets. The referenced ClusterRole is looked up in the complete ClusterRole inventory; ServiceAccount subjects and RoleBinding paths are out of scope.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_w.pass_when: The referenced ClusterRole has no rule matching the permission (or the ClusterRole is not present in the inventory).
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_w.fail_when: A non-system User/Group is bound and the referenced ClusterRole grants create, update or delete on validatingwebhookconfigurations/mutatingwebhookconfigurations (admissionregistration.k8s.io), including through '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_w.not_applicable_when: When the binding has no non-system User or Group subjects (only ServiceAccounts or reserved system: identities), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_client_.description: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration whose authentication block exists but authentication.x509.clientCAFile is unset or empty. Without a client CA the kubelet cannot verify x509 client certificates, so the API server's kubelet client identity cannot be authenticated and the kubelet API falls back to weaker or anonymous authentication.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_client_.fail_when: authentication is present but x509.clientCAFile is missing or empty.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_client_.not_applicable_when: When the configuration describes a component other than kubelet; a configuration without an authentication block is MANUAL.

k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_streami.description: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration whose streamingConnectionIdleTimeout is a Go duration where every numeric part is zero (e.g. '0' or '0s'). A zero timeout disables idle cut-off for exec/attach/port-forward streams, letting abandoned or hijacked interactive sessions stay open indefinitely and exhausting kubelet resources.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_streami.pass_when: streamingConnectionIdleTimeout is a valid duration with a non-zero component (e.g. 4h0m0s).
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_streami.not_applicable_when: When the configuration is not for kubelet; an absent field is MANUAL.

k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_strong_.description: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration whose tlsCipherSuites list is empty or contains any suite outside the CIS strong set (six ECDHE AES-GCM/CHACHA20 suites plus TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128/256_GCM). Weak suites such as 3DES or CBC-SHA let a network attacker downgrade or decrypt kubelet API traffic that carries exec streams and Pod logs.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_strong_.pass_when: tlsCipherSuites is non-empty and every entry is in the strong-cipher allow-list.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_strong_.fail_when: tlsCipherSuites is empty or contains a suite not on the allow-list.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_strong_.not_applicable_when: When the configuration is not for kubelet; an absent tlsCipherSuites field is MANUAL.

k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_tls_cer.description: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration that declares only one of tlsCertFile/tlsPrivateKeyFile while serverTLSBootstrap is not enabled. A half-configured serving certificate means the kubelet falls back to a self-signed certificate that clients cannot verify, enabling man-in-the-middle of kubelet API traffic.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_tls_cer.pass_when: serverTLSBootstrap is true, or both tlsCertFile and tlsPrivateKeyFile are non-empty.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_tls_cer.fail_when: Exactly one of tlsCertFile/tlsPrivateKeyFile is declared and serverTLSBootstrap is not true.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_tls_cer.not_applicable_when: When the configuration is not for kubelet; neither file declared (and no bootstrap) is MANUAL.

k8s.claude.cronjob.dashboard_not_deploye.description: Flags a CronJob whose regular containers (spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers[]) use a Kubernetes Dashboard image (path segment kubernetes-dashboard or kubernetesui/) or whose labels app, apps, k8s-app or app.kubernetes.io/name equal 'kubernetes-dashboard'. The Dashboard is a web UI frequently exposed with a privileged ServiceAccount; running it in each Job Pod the CronJob spawns on schedule provides an attacker-reachable path to cluster-wide read/write.
k8s.claude.cronjob.dashboard_not_deploye.pass_when: No regular container image matches the Dashboard pattern and no inspected label equals kubernetes-dashboard.
k8s.claude.cronjob.dashboard_not_deploye.fail_when: Any regular container image matches (^|/)(kubernetes-dashboard|kubernetesui/) or a Dashboard label is present.
k8s.claude.cronjob.dashboard_not_deploye.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.cronjob.no_privileged_port.description: Flags a CronJob where any regular container in spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec declares a ports[].containerPort below 1024. Binding a privileged port requires root or CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE inside the container, so the declaration signals that each Job Pod the CronJob spawns on schedule needs elevated privileges that would otherwise be unnecessary.
k8s.claude.cronjob.no_privileged_port.pass_when: Every declared containerPort is 1024 or higher.
k8s.claude.cronjob.no_privileged_port.fail_when: Any regular container declares a containerPort below 1024.
k8s.claude.cronjob.no_privileged_port.not_applicable_when: When no regular container declares any ports, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.cronjob.secrets_as_files.description: Flags a CronJob whose regular containers inject Secrets as environment variables, via env[].valueFrom.secretKeyRef or envFrom[].secretRef, in spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec. Environment-variable Secrets in each Job Pod the CronJob spawns on schedule leak through process listings, crash dumps, child processes and logging, and cannot be rotated without a restart, unlike mounted Secret volumes.
k8s.claude.cronjob.secrets_as_files.pass_when: No regular container references a Secret through env secretKeyRef or envFrom secretRef.
k8s.claude.cronjob.secrets_as_files.fail_when: At least one regular container uses env valueFrom.secretKeyRef or envFrom secretRef.
k8s.claude.cronjob.secrets_as_files.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); init and ephemeral containers are not inspected.

k8s.claude.daemonset.dashboard_not_deplo.description: Flags a DaemonSet whose regular containers (spec.template.spec.containers[]) use a Kubernetes Dashboard image (path segment kubernetes-dashboard or kubernetesui/) or whose labels app, apps, k8s-app or app.kubernetes.io/name equal 'kubernetes-dashboard'. The Dashboard is a web UI frequently exposed with a privileged ServiceAccount; running it in a copy on every node the DaemonSet schedules to provides an attacker-reachable path to cluster-wide read/write.
k8s.claude.daemonset.dashboard_not_deplo.pass_when: No regular container image matches the Dashboard pattern and no inspected label equals kubernetes-dashboard.
k8s.claude.daemonset.dashboard_not_deplo.fail_when: Any regular container image matches (^|/)(kubernetes-dashboard|kubernetesui/) or a Dashboard label is present.
k8s.claude.daemonset.dashboard_not_deplo.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.daemonset.no_privileged_port.description: Flags a DaemonSet where any regular container in spec.template.spec declares a ports[].containerPort below 1024. Binding a privileged port requires root or CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE inside the container, so the declaration signals that a copy on every node the DaemonSet schedules to needs elevated privileges that would otherwise be unnecessary.
k8s.claude.daemonset.no_privileged_port.pass_when: Every declared containerPort is 1024 or higher.
k8s.claude.daemonset.no_privileged_port.fail_when: Any regular container declares a containerPort below 1024.
k8s.claude.daemonset.no_privileged_port.not_applicable_when: When no regular container declares any ports, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.daemonset.secrets_as_files.description: Flags a DaemonSet whose regular containers inject Secrets as environment variables, via env[].valueFrom.secretKeyRef or envFrom[].secretRef, in spec.template.spec. Environment-variable Secrets in a copy on every node the DaemonSet schedules to leak through process listings, crash dumps, child processes and logging, and cannot be rotated without a restart, unlike mounted Secret volumes.
k8s.claude.daemonset.secrets_as_files.pass_when: No regular container references a Secret through env secretKeyRef or envFrom secretRef.
k8s.claude.daemonset.secrets_as_files.fail_when: At least one regular container uses env valueFrom.secretKeyRef or envFrom secretRef.
k8s.claude.daemonset.secrets_as_files.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); init and ephemeral containers are not inspected.

k8s.claude.deployment.dashboard_not_depl.description: Flags a Deployment whose regular containers (spec.template.spec.containers[]) use a Kubernetes Dashboard image (path segment kubernetes-dashboard or kubernetesui/) or whose labels app, apps, k8s-app or app.kubernetes.io/name equal 'kubernetes-dashboard'. The Dashboard is a web UI frequently exposed with a privileged ServiceAccount; running it in every replica the Deployment rolls out provides an attacker-reachable path to cluster-wide read/write.
k8s.claude.deployment.dashboard_not_depl.pass_when: No regular container image matches the Dashboard pattern and no inspected label equals kubernetes-dashboard.
k8s.claude.deployment.dashboard_not_depl.fail_when: Any regular container image matches (^|/)(kubernetes-dashboard|kubernetesui/) or a Dashboard label is present.
k8s.claude.deployment.dashboard_not_depl.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.deployment.no_privileged_port.description: Flags a Deployment where any regular container in spec.template.spec declares a ports[].containerPort below 1024. Binding a privileged port requires root or CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE inside the container, so the declaration signals that every replica the Deployment rolls out needs elevated privileges that would otherwise be unnecessary.
k8s.claude.deployment.no_privileged_port.pass_when: Every declared containerPort is 1024 or higher.
k8s.claude.deployment.no_privileged_port.fail_when: Any regular container declares a containerPort below 1024.
k8s.claude.deployment.no_privileged_port.not_applicable_when: When no regular container declares any ports, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.deployment.replicas_minimum_3.description: Flags a Deployment whose explicitly declared spec.replicas is lower than 3. With one or two replicas a single node failure, eviction or rollout leaves the service unavailable; an HPA-managed replica count is not considered.
k8s.claude.deployment.replicas_minimum_3.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); an omitted spec.replicas is UNKNOWN rather than the API default of 1.

k8s.claude.deployment.secrets_as_files.description: Flags a Deployment whose regular containers inject Secrets as environment variables, via env[].valueFrom.secretKeyRef or envFrom[].secretRef, in spec.template.spec. Environment-variable Secrets in every replica the Deployment rolls out leak through process listings, crash dumps, child processes and logging, and cannot be rotated without a restart, unlike mounted Secret volumes.
k8s.claude.deployment.secrets_as_files.pass_when: No regular container references a Secret through env secretKeyRef or envFrom secretRef.
k8s.claude.deployment.secrets_as_files.fail_when: At least one regular container uses env valueFrom.secretKeyRef or envFrom secretRef.
k8s.claude.deployment.secrets_as_files.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); init and ephemeral containers are not inspected.

k8s.claude.endpointslice.api_secure_port.description: Flags the EndpointSlice backing default/kubernetes (label kubernetes.io/service-name=kubernetes) when it has no ports or any port that is not named 'https' on 443 or 6443. A non-HTTPS or unexpected API endpoint port indicates the API server is reachable over an insecure or non-standard listener, exposing credentials and API traffic in cleartext.
k8s.claude.endpointslice.api_secure_port.pass_when: Every declared port is named https with port 443 or 6443.
k8s.claude.endpointslice.api_secure_port.fail_when: The ports list is empty or any port has another name or number.
k8s.claude.endpointslice.api_secure_port.not_applicable_when: When the EndpointSlice is not the default/kubernetes API slice, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.file_metadata.kubelet_conf_pe.description: Flags operator-supplied file metadata for /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf when its mode has any permission bit outside 0600 (group/other bits, execute, or setuid/setgid/sticky). This file is the kubelet kubeconfig, which holds the node's API client credentials; group- or world-accessible modes let other local users read secrets or tamper with kubelet behaviour.
k8s.claude.file_metadata.kubelet_conf_pe.not_applicable_when: When the file_metadata record describes a path other than /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.file_metadata.kubelet_config_.description: Flags operator-supplied file metadata for /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml when its mode has any permission bit outside 0600 (group/other bits, execute, or setuid/setgid/sticky). This file is the kubelet configuration file, controlling authentication, authorization and TLS of the kubelet; group- or world-accessible modes let other local users read secrets or tamper with kubelet behaviour.
k8s.claude.file_metadata.kubelet_config_.not_applicable_when: When the file_metadata record describes a path other than /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.file_metadata.kubelet_service.description: Flags operator-supplied file metadata for /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/kubeadm.conf when its mode has any permission bit outside 0600 (group/other bits, execute, or setuid/setgid/sticky). This file is the kubeadm systemd drop-in that defines kubelet startup arguments; group- or world-accessible modes let other local users read secrets or tamper with kubelet behaviour.
k8s.claude.file_metadata.kubelet_service.not_applicable_when: When the file_metadata record describes a path other than /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/kubeadm.conf, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_alia.description: Flags an Ingress carrying a snippet annotation whose value contains 'alias', evaluated only when the collector marked the annotation projection complete. An alias directive in a snippet can map an HTTP location onto arbitrary controller filesystem paths, exposing the controller's mounted token and certificates over HTTP.
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_alia.pass_when: No annotation matches the condition in a complete annotation projection.
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_alia.fail_when: Ingress has a snippet annotation whose value contains 'alias'.
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_alia.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); filtered annotations (annotations_complete != true) yield UNKNOWN.

k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_lua.description: Flags an Ingress carrying a snippet annotation whose value matches lua_, _lua or the literal 'kubernetes.io', evaluated only when the collector marked the annotation projection complete. Embedded Lua (content_by_lua_block etc.) executes arbitrary code inside the ingress-nginx controller process, giving cluster-wide Secret access.
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_lua.pass_when: No annotation matches the condition in a complete annotation projection.
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_lua.fail_when: Ingress has a snippet annotation whose value matches lua_, _lua or the literal 'kubernetes.io'.
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_lua.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); filtered annotations (annotations_complete != true) yield UNKNOWN.

k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippets.description: Flags an Ingress carrying any annotation whose key contains 'snippet', evaluated only when the collector marked the annotation projection complete. Snippet annotations (server-snippet, configuration-snippet, auth-snippet) inject raw NGINX configuration into the shared ingress-nginx controller; anyone who can write an Ingress can then read the controller's ServiceAccount token and Secrets of all namespaces (CVE-2021-25742).
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippets.pass_when: No annotation matches the condition in a complete annotation projection.
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippets.fail_when: Ingress has any annotation whose key contains 'snippet'.
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippets.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); filtered annotations (annotations_complete != true) yield UNKNOWN.

k8s.claude.job.dashboard_not_deployed.description: Flags a Job whose regular containers (spec.template.spec.containers[]) use a Kubernetes Dashboard image (path segment kubernetes-dashboard or kubernetesui/) or whose labels app, apps, k8s-app or app.kubernetes.io/name equal 'kubernetes-dashboard'. The Dashboard is a web UI frequently exposed with a privileged ServiceAccount; running it in each Pod the Job launches provides an attacker-reachable path to cluster-wide read/write.
k8s.claude.job.dashboard_not_deployed.pass_when: No regular container image matches the Dashboard pattern and no inspected label equals kubernetes-dashboard.
k8s.claude.job.dashboard_not_deployed.fail_when: Any regular container image matches (^|/)(kubernetes-dashboard|kubernetesui/) or a Dashboard label is present.
k8s.claude.job.dashboard_not_deployed.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

Binding a privileged port requires root or CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE inside the container, so the declaration signals that each Pod the Job launches needs elevated privileges that would otherwise be unnecessary.
k8s.claude.job.no_privileged_port.pass_when: Every declared containerPort is 1024 or higher.
k8s.claude.job.no_privileged_port.fail_when: Any regular container declares a containerPort below 1024.
k8s.claude.job.no_privileged_port.not_applicable_when: When no regular container declares any ports, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.job.secrets_as_files.description: Flags a Job whose regular containers inject Secrets as environment variables, via env[].valueFrom.secretKeyRef or envFrom[].secretRef, in spec.template.spec. Environment-variable Secrets in each Pod the Job launches leak through process listings, crash dumps, child processes and logging, and cannot be rotated without a restart, unlike mounted Secret volumes.
k8s.claude.job.secrets_as_files.pass_when: No regular container references a Secret through env secretKeyRef or envFrom secretRef.
k8s.claude.job.secrets_as_files.fail_when: At least one regular container uses env valueFrom.secretKeyRef or envFrom secretRef.
k8s.claude.job.secrets_as_files.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); init and ephemeral containers are not inspected.

k8s.claude.pod.capabilities_dropped.description: Flags a Pod where a regular container declares a securityContext.capabilities block that either adds any capability or drops none. Declaring capabilities without dropping any keeps the full container-runtime default set (including NET_RAW, CHOWN, SETUID), widening the kernel attack surface for container escape.
k8s.claude.pod.capabilities_dropped.pass_when: Each container either has no capabilities block, or its block adds nothing and drops at least one capability.
k8s.claude.pod.capabilities_dropped.fail_when: A container's capabilities block has a non-empty add list or an empty/missing drop list.
k8s.claude.pod.capabilities_dropped.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.pod.controller_manager_gc_thr.description: Flags a kube-controller-manager static Pod declaration whose --terminated-pod-gc-threshold flag is 0 or the 12500 default. At the default, up to 12500 terminated Pods accumulate before garbage collection, bloating etcd and slowing the API server; 0 disables GC entirely.
k8s.claude.pod.controller_manager_gc_thr.pass_when: Every kube-controller-manager declaration sets a numeric threshold other than 0 and 12500.
k8s.claude.pod.controller_manager_gc_thr.fail_when: Any kube-controller-manager declaration sets the threshold to 0 or 12500.
k8s.claude.pod.controller_manager_gc_thr.not_applicable_when: When the Pod contains no captured kube-controller-manager container, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); an undeclared flag is UNKNOWN.

k8s.claude.pod.cpu_limits_set.description: Flags a Pod where any regular container omits resources.limits.cpu. Without it an unbounded container can monopolise node CPU and starve co-located workloads (noisy-neighbour DoS).
k8s.claude.pod.cpu_limits_set.pass_when: Every regular container declares resources.limits.cpu with a scalar quantity.
k8s.claude.pod.cpu_limits_set.fail_when: At least one regular container has no resources.limits.cpu key.
k8s.claude.pod.cpu_limits_set.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); LimitRange defaults are not considered.

k8s.claude.pod.cpu_requests_set.description: Flags a Pod where any regular container omits resources.requests.cpu. Without it the scheduler cannot reserve CPU, so the Pod is placed on overcommitted nodes and is first to be throttled.
k8s.claude.pod.cpu_requests_set.pass_when: Every regular container declares resources.requests.cpu with a scalar quantity.
k8s.claude.pod.cpu_requests_set.fail_when: At least one regular container has no resources.requests.cpu key.
k8s.claude.pod.cpu_requests_set.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); LimitRange defaults are not considered.

k8s.claude.pod.dashboard_not_deployed.description: Flags a Pod whose regular containers (spec.containers[]) use a Kubernetes Dashboard image (path segment kubernetes-dashboard or kubernetesui/) or whose labels app, apps, k8s-app or app.kubernetes.io/name equal 'kubernetes-dashboard'. The Dashboard is a web UI frequently exposed with a privileged ServiceAccount; running it in the running Pod provides an attacker-reachable path to cluster-wide read/write.
k8s.claude.pod.dashboard_not_deployed.pass_when: No regular container image matches the Dashboard pattern and no inspected label equals kubernetes-dashboard.
k8s.claude.pod.dashboard_not_deployed.fail_when: Any regular container image matches (^|/)(kubernetes-dashboard|kubernetesui/) or a Dashboard label is present.
k8s.claude.pod.dashboard_not_deployed.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.pod.etcd_unique_ca.description: Compares the etcd static Pod's --trusted-ca-file path with every kube-apiserver --client-ca-file path in the complete Pod inventory and FAILs when they are the same file. If etcd trusts the cluster client CA, any certificate issued for Kubernetes clients (including kubelets) can authenticate directly to etcd and read or rewrite all cluster state and Secrets. Differing paths are MANUAL because certificate contents are not compared.
k8s.claude.pod.etcd_unique_ca.pass_when: Never PASS automatically: distinct paths yield MANUAL for content comparison.
k8s.claude.pod.etcd_unique_ca.fail_when: The etcd trusted-ca-file path equals a kube-apiserver client-ca-file path.
k8s.claude.pod.etcd_unique_ca.not_applicable_when: When the Pod is not an etcd declaration, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.pod.liveness_probe_configured.description: Flags a Pod where any regular container lacks a livenessProbe object. Without a livenessProbe the kubelet cannot detect a hung or deadlocked process and restart it, so failures persist silently.
k8s.claude.pod.liveness_probe_configured.pass_when: Every regular container declares a livenessProbe object.
k8s.claude.pod.liveness_probe_configured.fail_when: At least one regular container has no livenessProbe.
k8s.claude.pod.liveness_probe_configured.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); init and ephemeral containers are ignored.

k8s.claude.pod.memory_limits_set.description: Flags a Pod where any regular container omits resources.limits.memory. Without it a leaking or malicious container can consume all node memory and trigger OOM kills of other Pods or the kubelet.
k8s.claude.pod.memory_limits_set.pass_when: Every regular container declares resources.limits.memory with a scalar quantity.
k8s.claude.pod.memory_limits_set.fail_when: At least one regular container has no resources.limits.memory key.
k8s.claude.pod.memory_limits_set.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); LimitRange defaults are not considered.

k8s.claude.pod.memory_requests_set.description: Flags a Pod where any regular container omits resources.requests.memory. Without it the Pod gets BestEffort/Burstable QoS and is evicted first under memory pressure while the scheduler overcommits nodes.
k8s.claude.pod.memory_requests_set.pass_when: Every regular container declares resources.requests.memory with a scalar quantity.
k8s.claude.pod.memory_requests_set.fail_when: At least one regular container has no resources.requests.memory key.
k8s.claude.pod.memory_requests_set.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); LimitRange defaults are not considered.

k8s.claude.pod.no_added_capabilities.description: Flags a Pod where any regular container lists one or more entries in securityContext.capabilities.add. Each added Linux capability (e.g. NET_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, SYS_ADMIN) grants kernel privileges beyond the runtime default and is a common container-escape primitive.
k8s.claude.pod.no_added_capabilities.pass_when: No regular container has a non-empty capabilities.add list.
k8s.claude.pod.no_added_capabilities.fail_when: Any regular container adds at least one capability.
k8s.claude.pod.no_added_capabilities.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.pod.no_host_ipc.description: Flags a Pod whose spec.hostIPC is true, placing all its containers in the node's IPC namespace. A container sharing the host IPC namespace can read or tamper with shared memory segments and semaphores of host processes and other Pods.
k8s.claude.pod.no_host_ipc.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.pod.no_host_pid.description: Flags a Pod whose spec.hostPID is true, placing all its containers in the node's PID namespace. A container sharing the host PID namespace can see, ptrace and signal every process on the node, read their environments and pivot to host root.
k8s.claude.pod.no_host_pid.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.pod.no_host_ports.description: Flags a Pod where any regular container port entry contains a hostPort key (any value). hostPort binds the container directly on the node's network interface, bypassing Service/NetworkPolicy abstractions, colliding with node services and exposing the workload on every node address.
k8s.claude.pod.no_host_ports.pass_when: No regular container port declares hostPort.
k8s.claude.pod.no_host_ports.fail_when: Any regular container port declares hostPort.
k8s.claude.pod.no_host_ports.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.pod.no_literal_secret_env.description: Flags a Pod where a container (regular, init or ephemeral) sets an environment variable with a credential-like name (PASSWORD, SECRET, TOKEN, API_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY, ACCESS_KEY, etc., excluding names ending in _FILE/_PATH/_URL/_ID and similar references) to a non-empty literal value instead of valueFrom. Literal credentials are stored in plain text in the Pod spec and controller manifests, readable by anyone with get on the workload and persisted in etcd and Git. Only the value length is collected.
k8s.claude.pod.no_literal_secret_env.pass_when: No credential-like env name has a non-empty literal value.
k8s.claude.pod.no_literal_secret_env.fail_when: A credential-like env name has a literal value of length > 0.
k8s.claude.pod.no_literal_secret_env.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); a redacted value without a recorded length yields UNKNOWN.

k8s.claude.pod.no_net_raw_capability.description: Flags a Pod where any regular container adds NET_RAW, CAP_NET_RAW or ALL via securityContext.capabilities.add. NET_RAW allows crafting raw packets for ARP/DNS spoofing and traffic interception against other Pods on the node network.
k8s.claude.pod.no_net_raw_capability.pass_when: No regular container adds NET_RAW, CAP_NET_RAW or ALL.
k8s.claude.pod.no_net_raw_capability.fail_when: Any regular container's capabilities.add includes NET_RAW, CAP_NET_RAW or ALL.
k8s.claude.pod.no_net_raw_capability.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); the runtime-default NET_RAW that is not dropped is not flagged.

k8s.claude.pod.no_privileged_port.description: Flags a Pod where any regular container in spec declares a ports[].containerPort below 1024. Binding a privileged port requires root or CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE inside the container, so the declaration signals that the running Pod needs elevated privileges that would otherwise be unnecessary.
k8s.claude.pod.no_privileged_port.pass_when: Every declared containerPort is 1024 or higher.
k8s.claude.pod.no_privileged_port.fail_when: Any regular container declares a containerPort below 1024.
k8s.claude.pod.no_privileged_port.not_applicable_when: When no regular container declares any ports, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.pod.no_root_user.description: Flags a Pod where any regular container's effective runAsUser (container securityContext, else Pod securityContext) is explicitly 0. A container declared to run as UID 0 is root inside its namespace, so any breakout or writable hostPath lands as root on the node.
k8s.claude.pod.no_root_user.pass_when: No regular container resolves to runAsUser 0 (unset is accepted).
k8s.claude.pod.no_root_user.fail_when: Any regular container resolves to runAsUser 0.
k8s.claude.pod.no_root_user.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.pod.no_secret_env.description: Flags a Pod where any regular container environment variable is sourced from env[].valueFrom.secretKeyRef. Secret values in environment variables are exposed to every process in the container, to /proc/<pid>/environ readers and to crash/debug output; envFrom secretRef is covered separately by secrets_as_files.
k8s.claude.pod.no_secret_env.pass_when: No regular container env entry uses valueFrom.secretKeyRef.
k8s.claude.pod.no_secret_env.fail_when: At least one regular container env entry uses valueFrom.secretKeyRef.
k8s.claude.pod.no_secret_env.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.pod.no_windows_host_process.description: Flags a Pod where any regular container's effective securityContext.windowsOptions.hostProcess (container value, else Pod value) is true. A Windows HostProcess container runs directly on the Windows node as a host process with access to the host filesystem and network, equivalent to a privileged Linux container.
k8s.claude.pod.no_windows_host_process.pass_when: No regular container resolves to hostProcess=true.
k8s.claude.pod.no_windows_host_process.fail_when: Any regular container resolves to hostProcess=true.
k8s.claude.pod.no_windows_host_process.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.pod.readiness_probe_configure.description: Flags a Pod where any regular container lacks a readinessProbe object. Without a readinessProbe Services route traffic to the container before it is ready or after it degrades, causing request failures during rollouts.
k8s.claude.pod.readiness_probe_configure.pass_when: Every regular container declares a readinessProbe object.
k8s.claude.pod.readiness_probe_configure.fail_when: At least one regular container has no readinessProbe.
k8s.claude.pod.readiness_probe_configure.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); init and ephemeral containers are ignored.

k8s.claude.pod.run_as_user_10000.description: Flags a Pod where any regular container's effective runAsUser is undeclared or lower than 10000. Low UIDs can overlap with real host accounts, so a container escape or shared volume grants that host user's file access; an undeclared UID falls back to the image default, often root.
k8s.claude.pod.run_as_user_10000.pass_when: Every regular container resolves to an explicit runAsUser >= 10000.
k8s.claude.pod.run_as_user_10000.fail_when: Any regular container has no resolvable runAsUser or one below 10000.
k8s.claude.pod.run_as_user_10000.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.pod.runtime_default_seccomp.description: Flags a Pod unless its Pod-level securityContext.seccompProfile.type is RuntimeDefault or every regular container declares RuntimeDefault. Without the RuntimeDefault seccomp filter all syscalls are available, so kernel exploits (e.g. via unshare, keyctl, bpf) are reachable from the container. Localhost profiles are not accepted by this variant.
k8s.claude.pod.runtime_default_seccomp.pass_when: Pod-level type is RuntimeDefault, or all regular containers declare RuntimeDefault.
k8s.claude.pod.runtime_default_seccomp.fail_when: Neither condition holds (e.g. Unconfined, Localhost or unset on any container without a Pod-level RuntimeDefault).
k8s.claude.pod.runtime_default_seccomp.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.pod.secrets_as_files.description: Flags a Pod whose regular containers inject Secrets as environment variables, via env[].valueFrom.secretKeyRef or envFrom[].secretRef, in spec. Environment-variable Secrets in the running Pod leak through process listings, crash dumps, child processes and logging, and cannot be rotated without a restart, unlike mounted Secret volumes.
k8s.claude.pod.secrets_as_files.pass_when: No regular container references a Secret through env secretKeyRef or envFrom secretRef.
k8s.claude.pod.secrets_as_files.fail_when: At least one regular container uses env valueFrom.secretKeyRef or envFrom secretRef.
k8s.claude.pod.secrets_as_files.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); init and ephemeral containers are not inspected.

k8s.claude.podsecuritypolicy.allowed_hos.description: Flags a legacy PodSecurityPolicy whose spec.volumes permits hostPath (or '*') while spec.allowedHostPaths is empty. Pods admitted under it can mount any node path, e.g. / or /var/run/docker.sock, giving full host compromise.
k8s.claude.podsecuritypolicy.allowed_hos.pass_when: hostPath/'*' is not allowed, or allowedHostPaths lists at least one prefix.
k8s.claude.podsecuritypolicy.allowed_hos.fail_when: volumes includes hostPath or '*' and allowedHostPaths is empty.
k8s.claude.podsecuritypolicy.allowed_hos.not_applicable_when: When the cluster's Kubernetes version is 1.25 or later (PodSecurityPolicy API removed), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); missing version is UNKNOWN.

k8s.claude.podsecuritypolicy.default_sec.description: Flags a legacy PodSecurityPolicy whose annotation seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/defaultProfileName is not runtime/default or docker/default. Without a default seccomp profile, admitted Pods run Unconfined with the full syscall surface available for kernel exploitation.
k8s.claude.podsecuritypolicy.default_sec.pass_when: The default seccomp annotation is runtime/default or docker/default.
k8s.claude.podsecuritypolicy.default_sec.fail_when: The annotation is absent or set to another value.
k8s.claude.podsecuritypolicy.default_sec.not_applicable_when: When the cluster's Kubernetes version is 1.25 or later (PodSecurityPolicy API removed), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); missing version is UNKNOWN. Filtered annotations are UNKNOWN.

k8s.claude.podsecuritypolicy.security_se.description: Flags a legacy PodSecurityPolicy that neither sets spec.seLinux.rule to MustRunAs nor defaults AppArmor (runtime/default) or seccomp (runtime/default or docker/default) via annotations. Such a policy admits Pods with no mandatory-access-control confinement at all, removing a key layer against container breakout.
k8s.claude.podsecuritypolicy.security_se.pass_when: seLinux.rule is MustRunAs, or an AppArmor/seccomp default-profile annotation is runtime/default (docker/default for seccomp).
k8s.claude.podsecuritypolicy.security_se.fail_when: None of the SELinux, AppArmor or seccomp defaults is present.
k8s.claude.podsecuritypolicy.security_se.not_applicable_when: When the cluster's Kubernetes version is 1.25 or later (PodSecurityPolicy API removed), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); missing version is UNKNOWN.

k8s.claude.podtemplate.dashboard_not_dep.description: Flags a PodTemplate whose regular containers (template.spec.containers[]) use a Kubernetes Dashboard image (path segment kubernetes-dashboard or kubernetesui/) or whose labels app, apps, k8s-app or app.kubernetes.io/name equal 'kubernetes-dashboard'. The Dashboard is a web UI frequently exposed with a privileged ServiceAccount; running it in any Pod created from this PodTemplate provides an attacker-reachable path to cluster-wide read/write.
k8s.claude.podtemplate.dashboard_not_dep.pass_when: No regular container image matches the Dashboard pattern and no inspected label equals kubernetes-dashboard.
k8s.claude.podtemplate.dashboard_not_dep.fail_when: Any regular container image matches (^|/)(kubernetes-dashboard|kubernetesui/) or a Dashboard label is present.
k8s.claude.podtemplate.dashboard_not_dep.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.podtemplate.secrets_as_files.pass_when: No regular container references a Secret through env secretKeyRef or envFrom secretRef.
k8s.claude.podtemplate.secrets_as_files.fail_when: At least one regular container uses env valueFrom.secretKeyRef or envFrom secretRef.

k8s.claude.role.no_bind.description: Flags a Role whose declared rules allow the verb(s) bind on roles or clusterroles in rbac.authorization.k8s.io (a '*' in apiGroups, resources or verbs also matches). Such a grant lets any bound subject bind arbitrary Roles/ClusterRoles to any subject, bypassing RBAC escalation prevention to grant permissions the holder does not itself have within the Role's namespace. Only declared rules are read; bindings, aggregation and resourceNames narrowing are not considered.
k8s.claude.role.no_bind.pass_when: No rule combines a matching API group, resource (roles or clusterroles or '*') and verb (bind or '*').
k8s.claude.role.no_bind.fail_when: At least one rule matches the API group, resource and verb (bind on roles or clusterroles), including via '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.role.no_bind.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results), e.g. reserved system:/eks: names or rbac-defaults bootstrap roles.

k8s.claude.role.no_pod_create.description: Flags a Role whose declared rules allow the verb(s) create on pods in the core API group '' (a '*' in apiGroups, resources or verbs also matches). Such a grant lets any bound subject create Pods, which lets the holder schedule a Pod that mounts any ServiceAccount token, hostPath or privileged context in the namespace and so escalate to that identity or the node within the Role's namespace. Only declared rules are read; bindings, aggregation and resourceNames narrowing are not considered.
k8s.claude.role.no_pod_create.pass_when: No rule combines a matching API group, resource (pods or '*') and verb (create or '*').
k8s.claude.role.no_pod_create.fail_when: At least one rule matches the API group, resource and verb (create on pods), including via '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.role.no_pod_create.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results), e.g. reserved system:/eks: names or rbac-defaults bootstrap roles.

k8s.claude.role.no_secret_read.description: Flags a Role whose declared rules allow the verb(s) get, list or watch on secrets in the core API group '' (a '*' in apiGroups, resources or verbs also matches). Such a grant lets any bound subject read Secret objects, exposing ServiceAccount tokens, TLS keys and application credentials stored in the scope within the Role's namespace. Only declared rules are read; bindings, aggregation and resourceNames narrowing are not considered.
k8s.claude.role.no_secret_read.pass_when: No rule combines a matching API group, resource (secrets or '*') and verb (get, list or watch or '*').
k8s.claude.role.no_secret_read.fail_when: At least one rule matches the API group, resource and verb (get, list or watch on secrets), including via '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.role.no_secret_read.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results), e.g. reserved system:/eks: names or rbac-defaults bootstrap roles.

k8s.claude.role.no_wildcard_resources_or.description: Flags a Role with any rule whose resources entry contains a '*' character (e.g. '*' or 'pods/*') or whose verbs list contains the literal '*'. Wildcard grants silently extend to every current and future resource or verb, including Secrets, exec and RBAC writes, making the Role far broader than reviewed. apiGroups wildcards alone are not flagged by this variant.
k8s.claude.role.no_wildcard_resources_or.pass_when: Every rule lists explicit resources without '*' and explicit verbs without '*'.
k8s.claude.role.no_wildcard_resources_or.fail_when: Any rule has a resource string containing '*' or a verbs entry equal to '*'.
k8s.claude.role.no_wildcard_resources_or.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.service.no_tiller_labels.description: Flags a Service labelled app=helm or name=tiller, the labels of the Helm v2 Tiller service. Tiller exposes an unauthenticated gRPC endpoint (port 44134) that installs charts with its usually cluster-admin ServiceAccount, giving any in-cluster caller cluster takeover.
k8s.claude.service.no_tiller_labels.pass_when: Neither label app=helm nor name=tiller is present.
k8s.claude.service.no_tiller_labels.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.service.no_tiller_selector.description: Flags a Service whose metadata label keys or spec.selector keys contain the substring 'tiller' (case-insensitive). A Service routing to Tiller pods exposes the Helm v2 server API, which deploys arbitrary workloads with Tiller's privileged identity. Only keys are inspected, not label values.
k8s.claude.service.no_tiller_selector.pass_when: No label or selector key contains 'tiller'.
k8s.claude.service.no_tiller_selector.fail_when: At least one label or selector key contains 'tiller'.
k8s.claude.service.no_tiller_selector.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.cronjob.no_host_network.description: Flags a CronJob whose Pod template at spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec sets hostNetwork: true in its Pod template. For each Job Pod the CronJob spawns on schedule, the Pods share the node's network namespace, can bind node ports, sniff node traffic and reach node-local services such as the kubelet and cloud metadata endpoint.
k8s.cronjob.no_host_network.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.cronjob.no_host_ports.description: Flags a CronJob whose Pod template at spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec has any container (regular, init or ephemeral) with a non-zero ports[].hostPort. For each Job Pod the CronJob spawns on schedule, the container is published directly on every scheduled node's IP, bypassing Service and NetworkPolicy controls.
k8s.cronjob.no_host_ports.pass_when: All hostPort values are 0 or omitted.
k8s.cronjob.no_host_ports.fail_when: Any container declares hostPort between 1 and 65535.
k8s.cronjob.no_host_ports.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.cronjob.no_privileged.description: Flags a CronJob whose Pod template at spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec has any container (regular, init or ephemeral) with securityContext.privileged: true. For each Job Pod the CronJob spawns on schedule, a privileged container has all capabilities and host device access, so it can trivially escape to the node.
k8s.cronjob.no_privileged.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.cronjob.non_root.description: Flags a CronJob whose Pod template at spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec has any container (regular, init or ephemeral) whose effective runAsNonRoot (container, else Pod securityContext) is not true or whose effective runAsUser is 0. For each Job Pod the CronJob spawns on schedule, root containers turn any escape, writable mount or kernel bug into node root.
k8s.cronjob.non_root.pass_when: Every container resolves to runAsNonRoot: true and no runAsUser of 0.
k8s.cronjob.non_root.fail_when: Any container lacks runAsNonRoot: true or resolves to runAsUser 0.
k8s.cronjob.non_root.not_applicable_when: When spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.os.name is windows (Linux-only predicate), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.daemonset.no_privileged.description: Flags a DaemonSet whose Pod template at spec.template.spec has any container (regular, init or ephemeral) with securityContext.privileged: true. For a copy on every node the DaemonSet schedules to, a privileged container has all capabilities and host device access, so it can trivially escape to the node.
k8s.daemonset.no_privileged.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.daemonset.non_root.description: Flags a DaemonSet whose Pod template at spec.template.spec has any container (regular, init or ephemeral) whose effective runAsNonRoot (container, else Pod securityContext) is not true or whose effective runAsUser is 0. For a copy on every node the DaemonSet schedules to, root containers turn any escape, writable mount or kernel bug into node root.
k8s.daemonset.non_root.pass_when: Every container resolves to runAsNonRoot: true and no runAsUser of 0.
k8s.daemonset.non_root.fail_when: Any container lacks runAsNonRoot: true or resolves to runAsUser 0.
k8s.daemonset.non_root.not_applicable_when: When spec.template.spec.os.name is windows (Linux-only predicate), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.gap.apiserver.deny_service_external_.description: Flags a kube-apiserver static Pod declaration whose --enable-admission-plugins list does not contain DenyServiceExternalIPs. Without it any user who can create or update a Service may set spec.externalIPs and hijack traffic destined for arbitrary IPs from every node and Pod (CVE-2020-8554).
k8s.gap.apiserver.deny_service_external_.pass_when: Every captured kube-apiserver declaration lists DenyServiceExternalIPs in --enable-admission-plugins.
k8s.gap.apiserver.deny_service_external_.fail_when: A captured kube-apiserver declaration omits DenyServiceExternalIPs from --enable-admission-plugins.
k8s.gap.apiserver.deny_service_external_.not_applicable_when: When the Pod has no captured kube-apiserver container, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); an undeclared flag is UNKNOWN.

k8s.gap.apiserver.event_rate_limit.description: Flags a kube-apiserver static Pod declaration whose --enable-admission-plugins list does not contain EventRateLimit. k8s.gap.apiserver.event_rate_limit.fail_when: A captured kube-apiserver declaration omits EventRateLimit from --enable-admission-plugins.

k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_impersonation.description: Flags a ClusterRole with a declared rule granting verb impersonate (or '*') on users or serviceaccounts in the core or authentication.k8s.io group (wildcard resources included). Impersonation lets the holder send requests as any user or ServiceAccount, e.g. a cluster-admin identity, a direct RBAC escalation. Group and uid impersonation are not matched by this predicate; resourceNames narrowing is reported but still counts as a match.
k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_impersonation.pass_when: No rule matches the listed API group, resource and verb combinations.
k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_impersonation.fail_when: At least one rule grants verb impersonate.
k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_impersonation.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_pod_interactive_.description: Flags a ClusterRole with a declared rule granting create on pods/exec, pods/attach or pods/portforward, or patch/update on pods/ephemeralcontainers (core group, '*' and subresource wildcards included). These subresources run commands or attach debuggers inside running workloads, exposing their mounted ServiceAccount tokens, Secrets and network position; resourceNames narrowing is reported but still counts as a match.
k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_pod_interactive_.pass_when: No rule matches the listed API group, resource and verb combinations.
k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_pod_interactive_.fail_when: At least one rule grants create on pods/exec, pods/attach or pods/portforward, or patch/update on pods/ephemeralcontainers.
k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_pod_interactive_.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_service_status_w.description: Flags a ClusterRole with a declared rule granting update or patch on services/status (core group). Writing services/status lets the holder set status.loadBalancer.ingress IPs and redirect cluster traffic to attacker-chosen destinations (CVE-2020-8554); resourceNames narrowing is reported but still counts as a match.
k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_service_status_w.pass_when: No rule matches the listed API group, resource and verb combinations.
k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_service_status_w.fail_when: At least one rule grants update or patch on services/status.
k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_service_status_w.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_workload_control.description: Flags a ClusterRole with a declared rule granting create, update or patch on deployments/daemonsets/statefulsets/replicasets (apps), jobs/cronjobs (batch) or replicationcontrollers (core). Controller writes are equivalent to Pod creation: the holder can run a Pod with any ServiceAccount, hostPath or privileged setting in the scope and inherit its privileges; resourceNames narrowing is reported but still counts as a match.
k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_workload_control.pass_when: No rule matches the listed API group, resource and verb combinations.
k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_workload_control.fail_when: At least one declared rule grants create, update or patch on deployments, daemonsets, statefulsets or replicasets in apps; jobs or cronjobs in batch; or replicationcontrollers in the core API group (including matching wildcards).
k8s.htbp.clusterrole.no_workload_control.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.htbp.clusterrolebinding.no_anonymous.description: Flags a ClusterRoleBinding with a subject of kind User named system:anonymous. Any unauthenticated request to the API server (when anonymous auth is enabled) then receives the bound role's permissions, enabling unauthenticated cluster access. The system:unauthenticated group is covered by a different check.
k8s.htbp.clusterrolebinding.no_anonymous.fail_when: At least one subject is User system:anonymous.
k8s.htbp.clusterrolebinding.no_anonymous.not_applicable_when: When the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.htbp.secret.no_legacy_service_accoun.description: Flags a Secret whose type is kubernetes.io/service-account-token, i.e. a legacy long-lived ServiceAccount token. These tokens never expire and stay valid until the Secret is deleted, so a single leak gives permanent API access as that ServiceAccount; only metadata is read, never the token.
k8s.htbp.secret.no_legacy_service_accoun.pass_when: Secret type is anything other than kubernetes.io/service-account-token.
k8s.htbp.secret.no_legacy_service_accoun.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.htbp.service.no_external_ips.description: Flags a Service whose spec.externalIPs list is non-empty. kube-proxy captures traffic sent to those addresses from every node and Pod, so a Service author can intercept connections to arbitrary external IPs (CVE-2020-8554).
k8s.htbp.service.no_external_ips.fail_when: spec.externalIPs lists at least one address.
k8s.htbp.service.no_external_ips.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results) (e.g. the default/kubernetes API Service).

k8s.namespace.quota_limits_cpu.description: Flags a Namespace with no unscoped ResourceQuota whose spec.hard sets limits.cpu, using the complete ResourceQuota inventory. Without a namespace-wide cap on total CPU limits, one tenant or compromised workload can consume cluster capacity and starve other namespaces. A quota limited by scopes/scopeSelector only yields MANUAL.
k8s.namespace.quota_limits_cpu.pass_when: At least one ResourceQuota in the namespace without scopes/scopeSelector declares hard['limits.cpu'].
k8s.namespace.quota_limits_cpu.fail_when: No ResourceQuota in the namespace declares hard['limits.cpu'] at all.
k8s.namespace.quota_limits_cpu.not_applicable_when: When the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results) (kube-system, kube-public, kube-node-lease, provider namespaces); incomplete quota inventory is UNKNOWN.

Without a namespace-wide cap on total memory limits, one tenant or compromised workload can consume cluster capacity and starve other namespaces. A quota limited by scopes/scopeSelector only yields MANUAL.
